### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the three activities A19, A20 and A25 each took part in a substantial share of cases — about 33 in 100, 29 in 100 and 41 in 100 traces respectively, never twice within the same trace, so roughly one of the three ran per case. In the later window, each appears in only about 1 in 200 traces. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- In the earlier window, A27's outgoing transitions were split between A28 (about 52 in 100) and the three activities A25, A19 and A20 (together about 44 in 100); in the later window, about 97 in 100 of A27's outgoing transitions lead directly to A28. [DIR005]
- In the earlier window, A28's outgoing transitions were split between A29 (about 43 in 100) and the same three activities (together about 52 in 100); in the later window, about 97 in 100 lead directly to A29. [DIR006]
- In the earlier window, each of the three activities handed over almost exclusively to A28 or A29 (for example A19 to A29 in about 55 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and to A28 in about 42 in 100), placing them just before or just after A28; A28 was immediately followed by A25 in all 38 earlier observations of that pair. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG003]
- The step distances collapsed accordingly: A27 and A28 became immediately adjacent in about 98 in 100 later cases (about 52 in 100 earlier), A28 and A29 in about 96 in 100 (about 43 in 100 earlier), and the typical distance from A27 to A29 shrank from three event steps (about 90 in 100 earlier cases) to two (about 96 in 100 later). [LAG001, LAG004, LAG002]
- A27 and A29 still occur in every trace in both windows; A27's mean event position moved slightly later (0.46 to 0.48 of the trace) and A29's slightly earlier (0.57 to 0.55). [POS004, POS005]
- Separately, A10's outgoing transitions were redistributed: A15 fell from about 20 in 100 to about 6 in 100 and A47 from about 17 in 100 to about 6 in 100, while A26 (about 17 in 100) and A41 (about 9 in 100) appeared; this rests on only 35 versus 53 observed transitions. [DIR001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the alternative activities A19, A20 and A25, which in the earlier window executed in roughly one case in three or four each (about one of the three per case, placed immediately before A28 after A27, or immediately after A28 before A29), are effectively no longer executed in the later window, so that cases run directly from A27 through A28 to A29. The routing concentration at A27 and A28 and the contraction of the A27-to-A29 distance from three event steps to two each rest on essentially all 200 traces per window, and the participation drop is measured against 57–81 earlier occurrences per activity; with 18 qualifying items against roughly 0.5 expected for an unchanged process, the ensemble of differences is far beyond what random re-splits of these windows produce. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG004]

Limitations: zero participation only means the activities were not observed, so the evidence cannot distinguish a removal of the A19/A20/A25 block from these activities having become optional and executed extremely rarely (about 1 in 200 cases). The later-window profiles of the three activities themselves — their successors and positions — each rest on a single observation and carry no weight, and the many items largely describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS003]

Other differences: A10's outgoing transitions shifted away from A15 and A47 (each down to about 6 in 100) towards A26 (about 17 in 100) and A41 (about 9 in 100); with only 35 and 53 observed transitions, sampling variation in this low-traffic area is a competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out. [DIR001]
